You must focus on your strong suits. Reading up on homeschooling will do a lot more to answer your questions than I could in a post on Voat (while multitasking at work, haha). Basically, yes, not everyone can teach their kids all those things, that's why there are numerous choices one can make to address all of those issues to the best of one's ability. You can....

  1. Join a homeschool group - this can imply numerous things. Either just a meet up a few times a month to exchange ideas, to create a school like atmosphere when teaching your children, to exchange children (one homeschool parent I know will take on her friends 3 kids on top of her own 4 for one week out of the month and visa versa), to help tutor each other in subjects the parents themselves have issues with.

  2. Join one of the numerous online organizations that are made specifically to help homeschool parents (would definitely help in regards to subjects you have little grasp of. For me, that would be advanced math, though I plan on forcing myself to take classes to try and counteract that)

  3. Check in with your local school district and see what tools they have to offer your home student. Some will even allow homeschool kids to make use of the after school tutors (I feel that is more reasonable in rural areas like where I am).

  4. Enroll kids in after school programs just like you would if they were in school (addresses specifically the social interaction). Some school districts allow homeschool children to participate in school sports, but if not there are independent sport groups, like The Boys and Girls Club of America.

  5. Enroll kids in social activity programs, like Boy/Girl scouts.

  6. If you are religious (even if not) you can check in with your local religious organizations and see what sort of assistance they might lend to homeschooling (for example, one church near me randomly has days where a different one of the worshippers comes voluntarily and teaches parents/kids respectively. You must be signed up for these notifications, of course).

That's just a few suggestions. I am not religious, but I would still consider the options that involve churches as it does help alleviate some stress (I would like to think, lol).
